title: Incremental JSON-LD framed output SDK examples and tool-shim compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Ship SDK patterns and examples across TypeScript/Python/Go for emitting incremental JSON-LD framed outputs from streaming model responses, and provide a lightweight compatibility shim that maps legacy key/value structured events to JSON-LD frames for older clients. The goal is to standardize semantic structured output across SDKs while preserving backward compatibility with current tool-calling and streaming surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go SDK expose a thin API to emit/consume streaming JSON-LD frames with minimal allocation and predictable backpressure handling
Compatibility shim converts existing 'tool_event' and 'structured_output' envelopes into JSON-LD frames without losing critical metadata
Examples and integration tests demonstrating tool invocation + JSON-LD framed response, including mid-stream schema negotiation and graceful fallback to legacy envelopes
Benchmarks showing <=5% median token latency regression for typical short-turn interactions compared to existing streaming implementations
Documentation examples in the repo and a short migration guide for customers using structured_output or tool_event payloads
implementation_notes: Design: prefer JSON-LD framing to allow semantic tags (schema.org, custom context) for downstream consumers and event replay
Streaming model: emit compact JSON-LD frames per logical update (e.g., partial entity, property-set), with an optional 'frame_id' and 'final' flag
Backpressure: use existing SDK stream backpressure hooks; add an optional 'ack' callback for customers that need end-to-end durability semantics
Compatibility shim: two-pass parser that first tries JSON-LD context, falls back to legacy key-based envelopes and maps keys to @type/@context where possible
Trade-offs: JSON-LD increases bytes on wire; mitigated by context compaction and optional context share message at stream start
Security: ensure no arbitrary @context URIs are dereferenced by default; contexts must be whitelisted in config for private deployments
notes: Initial spike (2025-02-20) validated that JSON-LD framing can be emitted per token group without excessive CPU overhead on x86 and A10X GPUs
Prototype code included a 'context-announce' control message that reduces repeated context payloads by ~70% for typical prompts
PM feedback: emphasize migration path for customers that rely on existing structured_output keys in telemetry and billing pipelines
Design feedback: add a small validation helper in each SDK that verifies frames against a provided JSON-LD frame schema before emission
Ops note: Private deployments should default to a local context cache and reject unrecognized remote contexts unless explicitly allowed
migration_guide_outline: 1) Accept JSON-LD frames: show minimal change example in TS/Py/Go
2) Use compatibility shim: opt-in mapping to convert legacy tool_event to '@type' annotated frames
3) Enable context compaction: config options for stream-level context share
4) Validate frames: opt-in schema validation helper and sample tests
5) Rollout: start with canary customers, fallback to legacy envelopes on error
testing_plan: Unit tests: serializer/deserializer parity across languages
Integration: e2e tool-call -> model -> framed response -> consumer test harness
Performance: capture p50/p95 token latency across a suite of short and long-turn prompts
Compatibility: verify shim correctly maps at least 95% of existing structured_output keys used in our top 20 customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased payload size causing higher egress costs; Mitigation: context compaction and optional binary compression for dedicated/private tiers
Risk: clients may misuse JSON-LD @context to load remote resources; Mitigation: default to local policy and whitelist domains
Risk: ambiguous mapping from legacy keys to semantic types; Mitigation: maintain a mapping table and provide warnings in migration tests
